title: Shri Saurashtra Patel Seva Samaj included in World Book of Records for conducting 160 motivational Thursday sessions
excerpt: Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendrabhai Patel along with Gujarat’s Deputy Chief Minister Harshbhai Sanghavi, Union Minister Mansukhbhai Mandaviya, with ministers, legislators, industrialists, social leaders, trustees, and representatives of various organizations attended the grand ceremony.
content:
Gujarat/India: Shri Saurashtra Patel Seva Samaj, Surat celebrated a momentous occasion with the grand Lokarpan Ceremony of the newly developed Jamnaba Vidyarthi Bhavan, held in the distinguished presence of Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendrabhai Patel. The event marked a significant milestone in the organization’s longstanding commitment to education, social welfare, and community development.

Adding to the significance of the occasion, Shri Saurashtra Patel Seva Samaj was included in World Book of Records for successfully conducting 160 motivational Thursday sessions on the themes of Health, Wealth, and Happiness between 16 March 2023 and 21 May 2026 at Maniben Patel Chowk, Valak Junction, Surat. These sessions have played a vital role in inspiring individuals, promoting positive thinking, and encouraging social awareness within the community.

The prestigious recognition was presented by prominent representatives of World Book of Records including Santosh Shukla, CEO; Dr. Ashwinbhai Trivedi and Divyangkumar Gandhi, Chartered Officer, Gujarat. The dignitaries commended the organization for its outstanding contribution to youth motivation, educational advancement, health awareness, and community service.

Witnessed by a large gathering of community members and well-wishers, the newly inaugurated Jamnaba Vidyarthi Bhavan stands as a symbol of educational empowerment and social progress. The trustees and office bearers of Shri Saurashtra Patel Seva Samaj expressed sincere gratitude to all supporters and participants for contributing to the success of this historic event.
author: Editorial Desk

title: Securing Energy in an Uncertain World
excerpt: As energy security remains the global agenda, a delicate balancing act for governments — between rising demand, climate ambition, and geopolitical pressure on critical supply chains.
content:
The global energy landscape has never been more complex. Governments around the world are grappling with the twin imperatives of ensuring energy security while meeting ambitious climate targets. The geopolitical tensions of recent years have exposed the fragility of energy supply chains, pushing nations to reassess their dependence on imported fossil fuels.

In the Middle East, Gulf states are accelerating diversification efforts, channeling oil revenues into renewable energy projects and industrial development. Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 program has already yielded significant investments in solar and wind, while the UAE's Masdar initiative continues to develop clean energy projects across 40 countries.

Meanwhile, Europe's energy crisis has prompted a rethinking of energy policy priorities. The continent's rapid pivot away from Russian gas has accelerated investments in LNG terminals, domestic renewables, and energy efficiency measures. The EU's REPowerEU plan targets 45% renewable energy by 2030, up from the previous 40% target.

In Asia, energy demand continues to grow at pace with economic development. India's solar capacity has crossed the 100 GW milestone, while China continues to dominate global clean energy manufacturing. The International Energy Agency projects that Asia will account for over 50% of global energy demand growth through 2030.
author: Editorial Desk

title: OPEC+ Holds Output Steady Amid Demand Headwinds
excerpt: The cartel resists pressure to increase supply as economic slowdown clouds demand forecasts.
content:
OPEC+ members agreed to maintain current production levels at their latest ministerial meeting, resisting calls from consuming nations to increase output. The decision reflects growing uncertainty over global demand as major economies face headwinds from high interest rates and slowing growth.

Brent crude has been trading in a narrow band around $84 per barrel, reflecting the balance between supply discipline and demand concerns. Analysts note that the cartel's cohesion has been tested by members exceeding quotas, but core members Saudi Arabia and Russia appear committed to the current strategy.
author: Marcus Okafor

title: India's Solar Capacity Crosses 100 GW Milestone
excerpt: A historic milestone for the world's most populous nation as it races toward its 500 GW renewable target.
content:
India has achieved a landmark milestone in its clean energy journey, with cumulative solar installations crossing the 100 gigawatt mark. The achievement places India among an elite group of nations with over 100 GW of solar capacity, joining China, the European Union, and the United States.

The milestone was reached ahead of schedule, driven by aggressive tendering programs, falling technology costs, and supportive government policies. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has set an ambitious target of 500 GW of renewable capacity by 2030, of which solar is expected to contribute 300 GW.
author: Priya Sharma

title: Green Hydrogen Hub Announced in Gujarat
excerpt: India's western state will host one of Asia's largest green hydrogen production facilities.
content:
The Gujarat state government has announced plans for a major green hydrogen production hub, positioning the western Indian state as a key player in the global hydrogen economy. The project, backed by a consortium of domestic and international investors, aims to produce 1 million tonnes of green hydrogen annually by 2030.

Green hydrogen, produced by electrolyzing water using renewable electricity, is seen as critical for decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors such as steel, cement, and long-haul transport. The Gujarat hub will leverage the state's abundant solar resources and existing industrial infrastructure.
author: Arjun Patel

title: Battery Storage Costs Drop 18% Year-on-Year
excerpt: Rapidly falling costs are unlocking grid-scale storage deployments at unprecedented pace.
content:
The cost of lithium-ion battery storage has fallen by 18% over the past year, according to new data from Bloomberg NEF, continuing a decade-long trend that has made grid-scale energy storage increasingly competitive with peaker plants. The benchmark price for a battery energy storage system now stands at $142 per kilowatt-hour, down from $173 a year ago.

The cost reduction is being driven by overcapacity in Chinese battery manufacturing, improved cell chemistries, and supply chain optimization. Analysts expect further reductions of 10-15% over the next 12 months as new gigafactories come online globally.
author: Chen Wei

title: The Middle East's Next Decade of Energy Transition
excerpt: Gulf states accelerate diversification beyond hydrocarbons.
content:
Gulf Cooperation Council states are at a pivotal juncture in their economic and energy histories. Having built their prosperity on fossil fuel exports, they now face the challenge of transitioning to more diversified economies as the global energy system undergoes its most profound transformation in a century.

Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 program has already yielded significant results. The kingdom has awarded over 25 GW of renewable energy contracts, established NEOM as a showcase for sustainable city development, and diversified its economy through tourism, entertainment, and industrial development.
author: Rhea Menon

title: Why Grid Modernisation Is the Quiet Revolution
excerpt: Smart grids are reshaping how utilities forecast load.
content:
While much of the energy transition debate focuses on generation sources — solar panels, wind turbines, and batteries — the transformation of electricity grids is equally fundamental. Grid modernization, though less visible to the public, is enabling the integration of variable renewable energy sources and reshaping the economics of electricity supply.

Advanced metering infrastructure, distributed energy resource management systems, and artificial intelligence-powered grid optimization tools are being deployed at scale by utilities worldwide. These investments are improving grid reliability, enabling new business models, and reducing the cost of integrating renewable energy.
author: Daniel Kerr

title: Inside the Race for Lithium in Latin America
excerpt: Argentina, Chile and Bolivia compete to refine, not just mine.
content:
The lithium triangle — encompassing parts of Argentina, Chile, and Bolivia — holds more than half of the world's known lithium reserves. As electric vehicle adoption accelerates globally, demand for this critical mineral is surging, and the three nations are competing intensely for a larger share of the value chain.

Historically, Latin American nations have exported raw lithium carbonate and hydroxide, leaving higher-value processing and cell manufacturing to Asian producers. But a new wave of industrial policy is pushing Argentina and Chile to develop domestic battery industries, seeking to capture more of the economic value from their natural resources.
